requirements.text: Its name and version are `perigraph.collector` and `perigraph.collector_version`; the name SHOULD be one its author controls, such as a repository path or a domain, because comparisons that are collector-local key on it
A receiver MUST store every record it does not reject
A receiver MUST reject a record that names a part outside this list.
A collector MUST NOT withhold a record because parts are missing.
A collector MUST set `perigraph.status` to one of these:
Every failure path of a collector, including an exception raised inside it, MUST still emit a record with status `collector_failed`, because **a collector cannot record its own absence**.
A receiver MUST refuse a verdict over a record whose status is not `complete`, and MUST store it.
A collector that can lose records SHOULD report how many it lost, and a receiver MUST read a loss nobody reported as **unknown, never as zero**.

**A `pulled_by_us` part MUST carry its read lag in seconds, and a part with any other sourcing MUST NOT carry one.** The lag is a non-negative number: the time from the moment the collector read the fact to the moment it received the request, or zero if it read the fact after receiving the request.
So a receiver MAY let a pushed fact **widen** a verdict to `unknown` and MUST NOT let one narrow it.

**A receiver MAY let any claim it cannot check, whether a pushed part or a declaration that travels beside the record, trigger a refusal, and MUST NOT let one lift a refusal.** A forwarded model stamp is the one exception, and section 12.1 states the trust it requires.
A collector MUST emit each of the twelve parts and each of the four model parts as held or as absent.
Every absence MUST carry one of the reasons below, and the reason MUST name whose absence it is.
An absence that blames the collector MUST carry a detail: a measurement failure nobody described is one nobody can fix.
An absence that does not blame the collector MUST NOT carry one: there is no moment for us to describe.
When the body is not valid JSON, or is JSON that is not an object, a collector MUST give every manifest part read from the request body as `extraction_failed`.

A collector MUST NOT let a member outside the list, or one the list records nowhere, change any part, digest or identity, and MUST emit `perigraph.request.unlisted` and `perigraph.request.unlisted_omitted` (section 6) on every record of a request body that is a JSON object: a member nobody reads is a change nobody records, and dropping it silently would make its absence look clean.
The manifest MUST be static per collector version.
A receiver MUST refuse a verdict over a record with a contradiction in either manifest, because no absence in such a record can be read at face value.

It is an error to ask such a record for an identity, and a receiver MUST refuse a verdict over one, because an identity constant across every possible harness groups things that have nothing in common.
A digest MUST declare its boundary.
**Where several system messages are present**, a collector MUST join their contents with a single U+000A in the order they appear.
**A `parsed` digest is comparable only against another digest from the same collector at the same version.** A receiver MUST refuse a comparison across collectors or versions.
A `pushed_by_owner` declaration MUST be a string, and a collector MUST digest it at `canonical_value` as that JSON string, quotes included, so two collectors' declarations of one string compare too.
A collector MUST NOT canonicalise a `model_visible` payload before digesting it.
A collector MAY canonicalise a `parsed` payload.
A collector MUST serialise a `canonical_value` payload exactly as `digest.canonical_value_serialisation` says.

A collector handed a decoded value rather than text, such as an in-process shim handed the dictionary a client will serialise, MUST be handed the value after every merge the client performs (an `extra_body` included), and MUST treat it by the JSON data model: an object with string names, an array, a string, a finite number, `true`, `false` or `null`, where a language's sequence or mapping types that its JSON serialiser writes as an array or an object are those.
A collector MUST NOT digest a payload after transmission.
A collector MUST record it as an absence with reason `not_observable`, not as a part with that sourcing, so that the harness half has one encoding for it.

`tool_trace` — the calls that actually happened — is bytes the sender holds, and **MUST NOT key an identity anyway.** A per-run outcome is unique per run, so keying on it makes every pair of runs incomparable.
A response digest SHOULD be over the response **as rendered to the model**, which is a stable projection rather than the raw body.

**A receiver MUST refuse a comparison of two arms whose decisions were missing different facts.** Missingness is not a nuisance term: a fact that was absent for one arm and present for the other **changed which candidate was tried**, so part of the difference between them was caused by the gap rather than chosen by the policy.

**A receiver MUST refuse a comparison of two conversations of different turn counts as two prices for the same work.** The cache discount attaches to the shape of a request rather than to its text -- identical content measured a 0% cache rate as one long message and 99.9% as a growing conversation -- so most of the difference between a one-turn arm and a five-turn arm is the turn count.

**A receiver MUST refuse a statement of what an alternative would have cost when either side's `context_partitioning` is unrecorded.** That is **undefined rather than uncertain**, and the difference decides the remedy: an unmeasured quantity can be measured later from the same record, and an undefined one cannot, because the record does not contain the question.

**Records grouped as one arm MUST NOT be given one verdict when the distinct harness identities derived from them number more than one, or number one while some record has none.** The identities are the ones a receiver derives (section 6), not the ones a record states.
A receiver that gives a verdict over the records of one identity within the arm MUST say how many records of the arm it left out.

**A receiver MUST refuse one verdict over records grouped as one arm when, for a part in `uniform_within_arm`, two records hold it at `canonical_value` with different digests, or one holds it there and another has it absent as `not_provided`.** The parts are the pushed parts and `decoding`, which never key the identity and still change what is scored: R17b's H3, H4 and H6 sent one request body and differed in the caller's readout and in a declared retry.
When no record pair refuses and some record is unknown, a receiver MUST report `unknown` and MUST NOT report the arm admitted.

**A receiver MUST refuse one verdict over records grouped as one arm when their `perigraph.request.unlisted` sets or `perigraph.request.unlisted_omitted` counts differ, or when some records carry them and some do not.** Records that all lack the pair refuse nothing by this rule.

A receiver MAY widen a verdict over a record whose unlisted set is not empty, or whose omitted count is not zero, to `unknown`, and SHOULD state the unlisted names with any verdict it gives over such records.

**Two arms grouped under one name that carry more than one model identity, or some with one and some without, MUST NOT be given one verdict.** A retrain from the same script and seed agreed with its predecessor on 93.4% of labels; pooled, the rate describes neither.

**A claim bound to a model identity MUST NOT be applied to records that do not carry that model identity.** A certificate over answers from a model that no longer exists is a certificate over a different model.

**Two model identities from different collectors or collector versions MUST NOT be compared.** `precision` and `runtime` are each collector's rendering, so the same model can digest differently in two of them.
The first turn of a context MUST NOT report a cache read — nothing was in the context before it.
`perigraph.harness_identity`, `perigraph.model_identity` and `perigraph.artifact_identity` MUST each be **omitted** when the record has none.
A receiver MUST reject attributes whose `perigraph.spec_version` it does not implement, rather than parsing what it recognises.
A receiver MUST reject attributes that do not form a record of this version.
A receiver MUST NOT trim white space from a wire value before these checks.

Part names contain no commas -- they come from a closed vocabulary -- so the separator is unambiguous, but a reader MUST drop empty entries: splitting `""` on `","` yields a single empty string in every language tried, which is a manifest claiming a part named empty-string, and that refuses the whole record.
**The list is a set.** A collector MAY emit the names in any order and SHOULD NOT repeat one; a receiver MUST count a repeated name once and MUST compare two manifests as sets.

A member name is requester-controlled text, so a collector MUST write only names matching `unlisted_names.pattern`, MUST write at most `unlisted_names.max` of them, the first in ascending order of code units, and MUST count every other unlisted member in `perigraph.request.unlisted_omitted`.
A collector MUST write both attributes or neither: a body that is not a JSON object has every manifest part `extraction_failed` and carries neither.
A receiver MUST read a missing pair as unknown, never as empty.

**A collector that cannot observe the model says so.** A collector outside the process that loaded the model, with no stamp to forward or read back (section 9) -- a request adapter, or a router or gateway in front of an unstamped backend -- MUST emit each of the four model parts either as absent with reason `not_observable` (`perigraph.model_absent.<part>.reason`) or, where it has a name for that part (a provider's model name names `checkpoint` and no other part), as a part with sourcing `not_observable`, that name as its label, and no digest.
Such a collector MUST NOT emit a model or artifact identity.

A record with no model half at all does not conform (section 9) but is not refused: it is a hole nobody named (section 1.2), indistinguishable from the record of a collector that loaded the model and lost the stamp; a receiver reads it as unknown, not as `not_observable`, and MUST NOT refuse the record for it.
The changelog MUST list the inputs withdrawn.

**A collector MUST NOT emit two versions from one collector version.** If it can produce either, it is two collectors, and its `perigraph.collector` or `perigraph.collector_version` MUST say which one ran.

A receiver for which an obligation is **unreachable** -- it never performs the comparison the obligation is about -- MAY say so instead of implementing it, and MUST then **demonstrate** the unreachability in the material that claims conformance.

**A collector MUST reproduce `spec/fixtures/identity.json` and `spec/fixtures/canonical_value.json`, and a stamper MUST reproduce `spec/fixtures/model_identity.json`.** It is the only part of conformance that a second implementation cannot pass by agreeing with itself.
A collector MUST emit a **model half** on every record: each of the four model parts below, as a part or as a named absence; together they are what answered, as opposed to what surrounded it.
A collector MUST give `extraction_failed` for a path containing a tab or a newline
That record stays admissible: a receiver MUST NOT refuse it for having no model identity, and its claims are simply not bound to model bytes.
A receiver that reads lineage MUST read an incomplete chain as `unknown`, never as clean, and SHOULD refuse a verdict on a set when any document in the chain lists that set as `trained_on`.

Version 2 lineage has a single `parent`, so a `merge` of several parents cannot list them all; such a document names one parent, and a receiver MUST read the merge's other ancestry as missing, which is `unknown`.
A `detail` MUST NOT quote request content, credentials, tokens or URLs carrying secrets.
A collector MUST NOT put request content or secrets in one.
A collector MUST NOT write a member name in `perigraph.request.unlisted` that does not match `unlisted_names.pattern`, and MUST NOT write any value.
A collector MUST NOT digest altered content and present the digest as `model_visible`.
A receiver that stores records from several tenants SHOULD treat identities and lineage as data that links them, with the same access control as the runs themselves.
A receiver SHOULD bound the number of attributes and the length of strings it accepts.
A proposal to add a part, model part, sourcing value, absence reason, answer mode or attribute uses `docs/proposals/0000-template.md` and MUST include:
never keys an identity, and a receiver MUST NOT compare it as if it did;
MUST be ignorable: a receiver MUST NOT reject a record because it carries one.
Members outside the `perigraph.` prefix MAY be present and are not part of the record.

A line that is not a JSON object is not a record, and a receiver MUST count it as a lost record rather than skip it silently: SPEC section 1.1 reads a loss nobody reported as `unknown`, and a skipped line is a loss nobody reported.
The requester MAY add a top-level member `perigraph_template` to the body to declare which text of its non-system messages is fixed and where the item goes.

**Reading.** The collector MUST apply these checks, and any that fails makes `request_template` `extraction_failed`, with a detail that names a failed check and the index of the entry, fixed string or message, and never quotes a string (SPEC 12.3).

**Forwarding.** A collector that sends the body on MUST remove `perigraph_template` first, unless it is configured to send to a hop that reads the template, and MUST leave every other member's decoded value unchanged.
Until one exists, a collector reading such a request is not conformant for it, and SHOULD say so by giving every part it cannot map the absence `not_reachable` with a detail naming the request shape.
A collector SHOULD put the record on the span that represents the model call it describes: in OpenTelemetry's GenAI conventions the inference span, and in OpenInference the `LLM` span.
A collector SHOULD raise the span's attribute count limit, or put the record on a span of its own linked to the model-call span, when the two together could pass the limit.
A receiver reading a record from a span MUST refuse a verdict over it when the span reports a non-zero dropped attribute count.
